title: Navigation Engine Task Request
description: Structured task submitted by an orchestrator (e.g. n8n) to the generic navigation engine. Describes a single navigate -> observe -> decide -> act -> check-success run. This contract is domain-agnostic: nothing here is specific to automotive, GA4, or any brand.

taskId.description: Caller-supplied unique identifier for this task run, echoed back in the response.

objective.description: Human-readable, natural-language description of what the engine should try to accomplish. Consumed by the reasoning layer as guidance, not parsed for control flow.

startUrl.description: Absolute URL where the navigation loop begins.

allowedDomains.description: Optional allow-list of hostnames (or hostname patterns) the engine may navigate to, in addition to whatever the engine's own preflight domain-discovery phase proposes (see docs/architecture.md 'Preflight domain discovery'). A caller is never required to enumerate every domain/subdomain a journey might use -- when omitted, the engine determines an initial trusted set on its own: the exact startUrl hostname and any hostname sharing its Public Suffix List registrable domain that preflight discovers via redirects, the canonical URL, or on-page links. When present, every listed hostname is trusted unconditionally, on top of that discovery. Any navigation attempt outside the resulting combined set is blocked by the safety layer.

journeyType.description: Optional free-text hint about the kind of journey this task represents (e.g. "lead-generation-funnel", "pricing-comparison"). Purely advisory: blended into the same generic objective-relevance text-matching preflight domain discovery uses to rank candidate links, and otherwise not parsed for control flow or any domain-specific branching -- the engine must never special-case a specific journeyType value.

successCriteria.description: Ordered or unordered list of conditions the engine checks after each step to decide whether the objective has been reached.

captureModules.description: Task-specific capture modules to activate during the run. Each module is a pluggable unit that records evidence; the core navigation loop does not know what any of them mean.

maxSteps.description: Deprecated top-level convenience field. Prefer limits.maxSteps. Retained only for readability in examples; engine reads limits.maxSteps as the source of truth.

metadata.description: Optional free-form, non-authoritative key-value bag for orchestrator bookkeeping (e.g. requestedBy, market, campaign id). The engine must not branch its core logic on any value in here.

id.description: Stable identifier for this criterion, referenced in the response's progress reporting.

type.description: Kind of check the engine performs. New types are additive and must not require changes to the core loop.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of what this criterion checks, also usable by the reasoning layer. For semantic_page_match, this text is also blended into the vocabulary the criterion matches against the page (alongside the task's objective) -- keep it a plain description of the target state, not a selector or URL.

config.description: Type-specific parameters (e.g. { "pattern": "**/summary" } for url_pattern, { "selector": "..." } for element_present, { "minScore": 0.4, "signals": ["title","headings","interactiveElements"] } for semantic_page_match, { "match": { "event": "config_finished" } } for data_layer_event or { "match": { "en": "config_finished" } } for network_event -- see docs/n8n-integration.md "Generic success criteria"). For data_layer_event/network_event, "match" is a plain object of string key/value pairs every one of which must be present and equal (string-compared) on a candidate dataLayer entry or network-event evidence record for the criterion to be satisfied -- never a fixed vendor/event-name vocabulary, since the keys and values are entirely caller-supplied. Left open to keep new criterion types additive.

required.description: Whether this criterion must be satisfied for stop_success, or is informational-only for progress tracking.

group.description: Optional. Criteria sharing the same group value are alternatives: the group counts as satisfied once any one member criterion is satisfied, and is required for stop_success exactly when at least one member is (same required-unless-false default, applied at group level -- see $defs/successCriterion's required field and src/core/successEvaluator.ts's getMissingRequiredCriteriaIds). A criterion with no group is its own implicit singleton group, so omitting this field everywhere reproduces the previous AND-of-all-required-criteria behaviour exactly. See docs/n8n-integration.md "Alternative (OR) success criteria groups".

captureModule.description: Identifier of a registered capture module. The core engine treats these as opaque plugin names.

maxSteps.description: Hard ceiling on the number of navigate/act cycles before the run is stopped with a max_steps outcome.

maxBacktracks.description: Hard ceiling on the number of go_back actions before the run is stopped with a max_backtracks outcome.

maxDurationSeconds.description: Optional wall-clock budget for the whole run.

maxRepeatedActions.description: Number of times the same (action type + target) pair may repeat consecutively before loop detection stops the run.

allowedActions.description: Subset of the global action vocabulary this task is permitted to use. The engine must reject any decision selecting an action outside this list.

allowFormSubmission.description: Must be explicitly set true to permit any action that submits a form. Defaults to false (disabled).

allowPaymentOrPurchase.description: Always disallowed in v1. Present for forward compatibility only; the engine must reject a task where this is true.

allowPersonalDataEntry.description: Always disallowed in v1. Present for forward compatibility only; the engine must reject a task where this is true.

requireDomainConfirmationOnRedirect.description: If true, a cross-domain redirect that stays within allowedDomains is still logged as a notable event in the step log.

consentInteractionPolicy.description: How the reasoning layer may interact with a consent/preference control (see docs/architecture.md 'Blocker recovery'). Never a license to alter granular consent settings by guesswork, and never enforced by hardcoded CTA wording or a vendor-specific selector -- the engine gives the model this policy as plain instruction and additionally checks every decision's own self-reported consent classification against it deterministically (see task-response.schema.json's reasoningProviderDiagnostics.decisions[].consentControlIntent/consentPolicyCompliant) before it is ever dispatched, correcting or safely stopping a decision that contradicts the requested policy rather than ever silently applying the opposite one. Omitted means "reject_optional" (privacy-preserving default; never defaults to "accept_optional"). "reject_optional": prefer a control that declines or continues without granting optional/non-essential data collection, never one that grants broad/optional consent. "essential_only": same practical latitude as "reject_optional" (the engine has no generic way to distinguish a granular essential-only screen from a plain reject control) -- offered as a distinct value for a caller whose own policy language specifically calls for it. "accept_optional": an explicit, caller-opted-in instruction to actually grant optional consent when a control for doing so is visible -- not merely a last resort for unblocking a control that is otherwise reachable regardless of the consent choice made (e.g. so consent-gated analytics evidence can be captured); never the default. "do_not_interact": the model must never click any consent/tracking-preference control at all, even to dismiss a blocker.

maxAlternativeCandidatesPerDecisionPoint.description: Milestone-anchored recovery / Alternative Route Exploration: the bounded number of distinct candidates the engine may try at one recovery anchor's decision point before treating it as exhausted. Omitted means the engine's own default (3). Always subject to maxSteps/maxBacktracks/every other safety control regardless of this value -- never a way around them, only a cap on how many distinct route candidates one decision point may be given before recovery moves on.

allowSurfaceAdoption.description: Active surface tracking scaffolding (Phase 3 PR 2, see docs/architecture.md 'Active surface tracking'): explicit opt-in, matching the allowFormSubmission pattern -- a new tab/popup/drawer/modal is never adopted as the engine's active navigation context for a task that omits or sets this false. Omitted means false. As of PR 2, setting this true changes nothing yet: no PR before PR 3 wires an actual adoption path.

surfaceAdoptionDomainPolicy.description: Only meaningful when allowSurfaceAdoption is true, and only once a later PR actually adopts a surface. 'require_allowed_domain' (the default): an adopted surface's own navigation is held to this run's existing allowedDomains, exactly like the tracked page -- no relaxation at all. 'extend_trust_from_landing': an explicit, caller-opted-in relaxation that additionally trusts the hostname an adopted surface actually lands on (never one merely referenced/linked), on top of allowedDomains -- never the default, since it widens what a run may reach.

maxAdoptedSurfacesPerRun.description: Active surface tracking scaffolding (Phase 3 PR 2): non-task-relaxable-upward ceiling on how many distinct surfaces (beyond the tracked page itself) one run may adopt in total -- same bounded-and-generic pattern as maxAlternativeCandidatesPerDecisionPoint. Omitted means the engine's own small fixed default (5). Only meaningful once allowSurfaceAdoption is true and an adoption path exists (PR 3 onward).

maxSettleMs.description: Adaptive settling (see docs/architecture.md 'Adaptive settling'): optional per-task override for how long the engine's post-navigation/post-click settle wait may run before giving up on the page ever going quiet (DOM mutations and the interactive-element candidate count both stop changing). Every settle point in the engine (navigate, click, low-confidence re-observation) uses the same value. Omitted means the engine's own default (3000ms). Hard-capped at 10000ms regardless of what's requested here -- never a way to turn a slow page into an effectively unbounded per-step hang.

actionType.description: Controlled action vocabulary. The reasoning layer selects one of these per step; it never generates arbitrary Playwright code.
